content: Camp Sweeney is a summer camp located in Gainesville, Texas, specifically designed for children with Type 1 diabetes, and occasionally their siblings. It has been operational since 1950. While it offers traditional summer camp activities such as swimming, hiking, archery, basketball, volleyball, water park fun, broadcasting, and arts and crafts, the camp is uniquely tailored to meet the needs of diabetic children. The camp is equipped with built-in blood glucose testing stations scattered throughout the premises, and counselors are always prepared with glucose monitors and insulin. During meals, each camper receives a food tray carefully prepared with the appropriate amount of carbohydrates tailored to their dietary needs. Additionally, campers attend medical lectures several times a week to learn how to better manage their diabetes and stay informed about the latest advancements in diabetes research. Camp Sweeney serves children aged 5 to 18, organizing them into age-appropriate cabins. Campers have the freedom to choose the activities they wish to participate in during the day. Counselors, often college students recruited from institutions like the University of Notre Dame and other universities nationwide, assist younger children in learning how to administer their own insulin injections or change their insulin pump sites. The primary goal of Camp Sweeney is to help children with diabetes develop healthy habits that they can maintain after leaving camp. It also fosters lasting relationships among children who share similar challenges associated with managing diabetes. Research conducted by the camp’s parent organization, the Southwestern Diabetic Foundation, has shown that children and young adults who attend Camp Sweeney experience a significant reduction in their HbA1c levels (a measure of blood glucose control), with an average decrease of approximately one full point after attending a standard 20-day session. Beyond diabetes management, Camp Sweeney aims to build self-confidence and create lifelong friendships. Many campers view the camp as more than just a summer program—it is a transformative experience that profoundly impacts their lives. Camp Sweeney is often described as a family, a place where campers feel a deep sense of belonging and support. In addition to its three 20-day summer sessions, Camp Sweeney offers a one-week senior week, a five-day mini session, a family weekend in the spring, and a five-day winter session. The camp is also home to an FCC-licensed non-commercial radio station, KPFC-FM. Campers and staff often express their love for Camp Sweeney through heartfelt quotes and testimonials, emphasizing the unique sense of community and acceptance they experience there. The camp is described as a place where individuality is celebrated, and everyone feels at home. Camp traditions, such as singing the camp song in a circle with hands joined, are performed in reverence and in memory of past campers and staff who have been part of the program. The camp song reflects the values of perseverance, faith, and courage, and it is a cherished part of the Camp Sweeney experience.
